bottleneck: Dopamine, serotonin, and other neuromodulators reconfigure entire brain circuits on timescales from milliseconds to hours, but how these broadcast signals interact with fast synaptic computation is poorly understood. Psychiatric drugs target these systems crudely — SSRIs bathe the whole brain in serotonin for weeks hoping the right circuits adapt — because no model predicts what precise modulation a given circuit needs. Neuromodulators act through volume transmission, receptor diversity, and second-messenger cascades that current theory cannot integrate with spike-based computation. The brain's volume-control knobs are turned blindly.
current_state: New fluorescent sensors map neuromodulator release in behaving animals, but a predictive theory of how modulation reshapes computation remains distant.

title: Neuromodulatory dynamics lack predictive theory
why_it_blocks: Every psychiatric drug works through these systems. Without understanding modulation, psychopharmacology stays at the level of flooding the brain and hoping — which is why antidepressants take weeks and fail a third of patients.
